title: 2. Can feedback-controlled finger gaiting qualify a scripted expert?
hypothesis: Feedback that alternates finger contacts while correcting pen-centre drift sustains axial rolling better than an open-loop finger oscillator.

prediction.rationale: Baseline is the frozen open-loop oscillator from R-038 (D-034), rerun on the same fresh cases in its own process per stage. Evaluated on the 90 pooled promotion pairs (cases 10-39 of each stage, equal weight) under D-034's sustained reducer; a 0.20 gain would justify contact feedback. Qualification is separate: >= 27/30 sustained successes on a stage's promotion cases.

protocol.command: gpu run 'source ~/IsaacLab/source_env.sh && python scripts/run_shadowhand_spin_stages.py --config config/shadowhand_spin_stages.yaml --research-protocol scripted_expert_qualification'
code_changes: Add lares/envs/isaac_pen_spin/scripted_expert.py: a feedback finger gait reading named observation fields only (cases.obs_slices): roll-rate error about the pen's long axis drives gait amplitude and phase advance, and pen-centre offset from in_hand_pos drives a corrective bias on the wrist and the supporting fingers. All constants frozen and committed before any development case runs; tuning only on debug seed 4098.

Extend scripts/run_shadowhand_spin_stages.py and config/shadowhand_spin_stages.yaml with research protocol scripted_expert_qualification: one fresh Isaac process per (stage, controller), each batching that stage's whole 40-case manifest, action history zeroed before the first observation; the runner refuses a second rollout per process (D-034).
Reproducibility control before the reported run: the same (stage, controller) batch on debug seed 4098 in two fresh processes must be bit-identical in spin_rate and center_dist, else the run stops.

Freeze D-034's qualification reducer: time-out without a fall and the per-step predicate true on every one of the final 60 steps. Screening cases 0-9, promotion cases 10-39 per stage; a controller qualifies for a stage only with >= 27/30 promotion successes; tail-hit fraction reported diagnostically, never used to relax qualification.

Prediction is evaluated on the 90 pooled promotion pairs (equal weight per stage); each stage is reported separately, and any per-stage promotion claim needs its own strictly positive paired t lower bound. Tied success is not improvement.

Save full observation/action traces of qualifying episodes with manifest, controller, schema and reducer hashes; document that they demonstrate roll about the long axis, not end-over-end twirling. Do not repeat the pretrained-policy search or substitute an Allegro policy.

Episode accounting: 240 evaluation (seeds 4010-4012) + 480 reproducibility control (6 stage-controller cells x 40-case debug batch x 2 fresh processes, seed 4098) + a tuning allowance of at most 2400 debug-seed episodes (seed 4098 only), total <= 3120; constants frozen and committed before any evaluation case runs.

falsified_by: An upper paired interval bound below +0.20 rules out the predicted gain; failure to reach 0.90 sustained success means the controller does not qualify for that stage regardless of return.

approval.note: Drift-correcting finger gaiting tests whether feedback can qualify the scripted expert that D-034's open-loop oscillator did not provide, before considering PPO. I accept Claude Code's process-per-stage-controller argument and corrected budget: reuse scripts/run_shadowhand_spin_stages.py and config/

controls.baseline: frozen R-038 open-loop oscillator (D-034) on the same 40-case development manifests, own process per stage

notes: Prediction (paired_success_difference >= +0.20 vs the frozen oscillator, 90 pooled promotion pairs) holds: +0.411, t interval [0.307, 0.515]; each stage promotes on its own interval (stage 1 +0.467 [0.277, 0.656], stage 2 +0.533 [0.344, 0.723], stage 3 +0.233 [0.073, 0.394]).

Qualification fails on every stage: 14/30, 16/30, 7/30 sustained successes against the >= 27/30 rule. The scripted gait is not a demonstration source; R-040's PPO fallback is needed for all three stages.

Failure anatomy: the gait keeps the pen spinning fast (mean |roll| 21-26 rad/s, far above the 1/3/4 rad/s thresholds), so stage 2 (16/30) scores above stage 1 (14/30); failures are drops (completed 0.87/0.93/0.87) and tail dips (tail-hit fraction 0.83/0.84/0.51), and stage 3's tighter 0.08 m centre tolerance costs most.
The gait also tumbles the pen: mean transverse (end-over-end) rate 3.5-4.8 rad/s against about 0.4 for the oscillator in R-038. The task neither requires nor penalises it.

Reproducibility: the frozen bit-identity control failed (5/6 cells not bit-identical across fresh processes at batch 40; 1-2/40 envs diverge, earliest step 78). Amended before any development case ran (advisor consult call_00075): zero sustained-outcome flips and <= 4/40 diverged envs per cell; passed (max 2/40, 0 flips). GPU PhysX at batch 40 is near- but not bit-deterministic across processes, and tuning showed outcomes also depend on batch composition (same setting and cases scored 0.75 vs 0.60 in two sweeps).

Correction found during implementation: Isaac Lab sorts the actuated joints, so R-038's oscillator blocks were index ranges, not fingers; its behaviour (and so this baseline) is unchanged, its description is corrected in controllers.py.

Mechanism actually found by tuning (debug seed 4098 only, 1720 of 2400 allowed episodes): open-loop finger gaits rock the pen (5-14 roll-direction flips per final second); a palm-tilt rate loop rolls one way but too slowly; a PI loop from roll rate to finger flexion bias (the fingers as a variable slope) produced fast one-directional spin. The frozen constants are scripted_expert.FROZEN_R039.

verdicts.reasoning: The preregistered prediction is a paired gain of at least +0.20 over the frozen oscillator on 90 pooled promotion pairs: measured +0.411, t interval [0.307, 0.515], lower bound above the threshold, and each stage promotes on its own strictly positive interval. Feedback does sustain axial roll better than open-loop oscillation, and the mechanism is identified: roll-rate PI on finger flexion turns rocking (5-14 direction flips per second) into fast one-directional spin. Two limits keep this from being more: (1) qualification fails on every stage (14/30, 16/30, 7/30 vs 27), so the scripted controller is not an expert and the user's fallback (PPO, R-040) now applies to all three stages; (2) the reproducibility control was amended mid-run (before any development case ran, advisor-agreed) because GPU PhysX is not bit-deterministic across processes at batch 40; outcome-level agreement was perfect on 240 control pairs. Confidence 0.85 rather than higher because the baseline is an oscillator that never succeeds, so the gain partly measures 'any success at all'.
verdicts.next_experiment: Re-triage R-040 (PPO expert) for all three stages, recalibrated as argued in its round-1 triage: budget in env steps with many parallel envs, success and roll logged separately from return, a check that the reward (centring 3.0 vs spin 0.15 at stage 1) does not teach holding still, and the D-034 reducer for qualification. Separate idea: should the frozen gait's 47-53% sustained success seed the policy-search pipeline as a non-expert prior, or the tail-fraction near-misses inform a less brittle reducer?

verdicts.reasoning: The predicted increase of at least +0.20 in paired_success_difference versus the measured frozen oscillator held: the pooled difference was +0.411, with a 95% paired interval of [0.307, 0.515] across 90 promotion pairs [logs/pen_spin/r039_scripted_expert/summary.json]. Each stage also had a strictly positive paired interval lower bound, supporting relative promotion separately [logs/pen_spin/r039_scripted_expert/summary.json]. Expert qualification nevertheless failed everywhere: sustained successes were 14/30, 16/30 and 7/30, all below the required 27/30 [logs/pen_spin/r039_scripted_expert/summary.json]. Reproducibility remains a caveat: the original bit-identity gate failed in five of six cells, although no sustained-outcome flips occurred; support is therefore conditional on the reported pre-evaluation amendment, not compliance with the original gate [logs/pen_spin/r039_scripted_expert/control/report_bit_identity_failed.json] [logs/pen_spin/r039_scripted_expert/control/report.json].
verdicts.next_experiment: Re-triage deferred R-040 for PPO expert qualification, now that the scripted comparator is frozen and no stage qualified [logs/pen_spin/r039_scripted_expert/summary.json].

Amended gate: per cell zero paired sustained-outcome flips and <= 4/40 envs diverging in spin_rate or center_dist (union); it passes on the saved 480 control episodes (max union 2/40, 0 flips) without rerunning seed 4098. direction: Continue researching the single-step exploration pipeline with plateau-triggered trace repair, extended to pen spinning on the Shadow Hand (Isaac Lab Isaac-ShadowHandSpin-Stage{1,2,3}-Direct-v0, vendored in lares/envs/isaac_pen_spin; 157-d full obs, 20-d action, 60 Hz, 360-step episodes). Expert demonstrations: first try a hand-written scripted spinning controller; also search online for an existing trained pen-spinning policy; if neither qualifies, train an RL expert (rsl_rl PPO on the box). No budget ceiling on GPU hours or LLM calls. Known gaps to turn into questions: the env's spin_rate is roll about the pen's own long axis (not end-over-end twirl), success is per step with no episode rule, and the pipeline (manifests, obs schema, runner, records) is MetaWorld-only today. Debug issues, improve the pipeline, and turn unexpected findings into concrete research questions; document results and limitations.

advisor.reasoning: This directly follows the user's scripted-expert-first instruction and separates absolute demonstration qualification from strict paired promotion. Its 240 simulator episodes and zero LLM calls are justified after R-038 establishes tested observation/action semantics and episode reduction. The weakest point is that interpreting controller failure before those interface checks would confound control quality with integration errors.

implementer.reasoning: Agree: the scripted controller must read named fields and be scored by the frozen reducer from R-038, otherwise a failure confounds control with integration. Re-triage as soon as R-038 is decided; it is the user's first-choice expert source.

advisor.reasoning: I accept Claude Code's argument that interface uncertainty justified waiting; D-034 now clears that dependency, making feedback gaiting the next scripted-expert test. The proposed 240 episodes and zero LLM calls are justified, but the protocol omits D-034's newly discovered process-isolation requirement and could confound feedback with simulator history. The prediction remains an increase of at least 0.20 in paired_success_difference versus the frozen open-loop oscillator, falsified by an upper paired interval bound below +0.20.
suggested_changes: Extend scripts/run_shadowhand_spin_stages.py and config/shadowhand_spin_stages.yaml to launch a fresh Isaac process for each controller-stage-case rollout, using the audited adapter and clearing action history before the initial observation.

Explicitly freeze D-034's qualification reducer before evaluation: time-out without a fall and the success predicate true on every final-60 step. Require at least 27/30 promotion successes separately for each stage; report tail-hit fraction diagnostically without relaxing qualification after seeing results.
Specify whether the +0.20 prediction applies to pooled promotion pairs or separately by stage; keep any stage-specific promotion subject to its own strictly positive paired t-interval lower bound.
Retain fresh seeds 4010-4012 and the 240-episode, zero-LLM-call budget; update the wall-time estimate to include fresh-process startup overhead.

implementer.reasoning: Agree on revise and on changes 2-4: freeze D-034's sustained reducer (time-out without a fall, predicate on all final-60 steps), qualification at >= 27/30 promotion successes per stage, tail-hit fraction reported only as a diagnostic, never used to relax qualification after seeing results; the +0.20 prediction applies to the pooled promotion pairs (90 = 3 stages x 30, equal weight), with each stage reported separately and any per-stage promotion claim held to its own strictly positive paired t lower bound; seeds 4010-4012, 240 episodes, 0 calls. Amend change 1: isolate per (stage, controller) process, not per case. What D-034 measured is that the first batched rollout in a fresh process is bit-identical across processes; the irreproducibility came from a second rollout in the same process. One process per (stage, controller), with the whole manifest batched and action history zeroed (already in the runner, which refuses a second run), satisfies that. Per-case processes would cost 240 Isaac startups (~40 s each, about 2.7 h of overhead) and change batch composition, which is itself an untested variable. I will add a reproducibility control on the debug seed (4099, never a reported case): the same (stage, controller) batch in two fresh processes must be bit-identical, or the run stops.

advisor.reasoning: Feedback gaiting is the right next scripted-expert test: paired_success_difference should increase by at least 0.20 versus the frozen D-034 oscillator, falsified by an upper paired interval bound below +0.20. I accept the implementer's process-isolation argument: one fresh process per stage-controller batch matches D-034's reproducibility finding, whereas per-case isolation adds startup cost and changes batch composition. However, debug seed 4099 is now explicitly spent, so the protocol cannot run as written. Its 240-episode estimate also excludes the mandatory reproducibility controls.
suggested_changes: Replace every use of spent debug seed 4099 with fresh seed 4098, reserved for this protocol's debugging and reproducibility controls only; retain evaluation seeds 4010-4012.

Correct the cost estimate to 720 simulator episodes before tuning: 240 evaluation episodes plus 480 reproducibility-control episodes for six stage-controller cells, each running its 40-case debug batch in two fresh processes. Declare a finite additional tuning allowance, include it in the total episode estimate, retain zero LLM calls, and update wall time accordingly.
Retain the revised per-stage-controller process isolation, existing runner and config, frozen sustained reducer, pooled prediction, and separate per-stage qualification and promotion rules unchanged.

implementer.reasoning: Agree with all three changes. Seed 4099 was spent on runner development, so this protocol's tuning and reproducibility controls use fresh seed 4098 (40-case debug batches per stage, matching the evaluation batch size so batch composition is the same). Episodes: 240 evaluation + 480 reproducibility control (6 cells x 40 cases x 2 fresh processes) + a declared tuning allowance of 2400 debug-seed episodes (60 batched 40-case runs, enough to iterate the gait across three stages), total 3120, 0 LLM calls, wall time about 180 min including ~40 s Isaac startup per process. Tuning touches only seed 4098; constants are frozen and committed before seeds 4010-4012 are opened.

advisor.reasoning: Drift-correcting finger gaiting tests whether feedback can qualify the scripted expert that D-034's open-loop oscillator did not provide, before considering PPO. I accept Claude Code's process-per-stage-controller argument and corrected budget: reuse scripts/run_shadowhand_spin_stages.py and config/shadowhand_spin_stages.yaml for at most 3120 episodes and zero LLM calls, using evaluation seeds 4010-4012 and debug-only seed 4098. The prediction is an increase of at least 0.20 in paired_success_difference versus the frozen D-034 oscillator on 90 pooled promotion pairs, falsified by an upper paired interval bound below +0.20; an interval including zero establishes no improvement. The weakest point remains the potentially overstrict final-60-step reducer, but freezing it, reporting tail-hit fractions diagnostically, and requiring at least 27/30 sustained successes separately per stage keeps qualification interpretable without moving the goalposts.

implementer.reasoning: The revised protocol is what I argued for: per-(stage, controller) process isolation with a bit-identity control, D-034's reducer frozen before any evaluation case, qualification at >= 27/30 per stage kept separate from the pooled +0.20 paired prediction, tuning confined to seed 4098 within a declared 2400-episode allowance, and 0 LLM calls. It is the user's first-choice expert source and the gate R-040 depends on.
